children: U.S. women's apparel retailer's Q2 net sales fell 12%, missing analyst expectations
Q2 adjusted EBITDA beat consensus, helped by $11.1 mln IEEPA tariff refund benefit
Company raised full-year outlook to include tariff refund benefit recognized in Q2
Torrid sees Q3 net sales between $230 mln and $235 mln
Company expects Q3 adjusted EBITDA between $15 mln and $20 mln
Torrid raises FY2026 outlook to reflect IEEPA tariff refund; underlying outlook unchanged
TARIFF REFUND - Q2 adjusted EBITDA benefited from $11.1 mln IEEPA tariff refund recorded as reduction in cost of goods sold
MERCHANDISING CHANGES - Improved sales trends late in Q2 attributed to better balance of core and fashion assortments and stronger footwear inventory, per CEO Lisa Harper

CUSTOMER STRATEGY - Early traction from customer growth initiatives, including expansion into third-party marketplaces and opening price point strategy, helped drive conversion and value perception, per CEO Lisa Harper
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "hold" and the breakdown of recommendations is 1 "strong buy" or "buy", 5 "hold" and 1 "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the apparel & accessories retailers peer group is "buy."
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Torrid Holdings Inc is $1.80, about 20.7% below its September 2 closing price of $2.27
